newsitem.title: JAPAN: YAMAICHI PRESIDENT SAYS NOT INVOLVED IN SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: YAMAICHI PRESIDENT SAYS NOT INVOLVED IN SCANDAL.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd's outgoing president Atsuo Miki told reporters on Monday that he was not involved in a corporate racketeer payoff scandal that has ensnared the brokerage.
The brokerage's outgoing chairman, Tsugio Yukihira also said he was not involved in the scandal.
Yamaichi announced on Monday that the two top executives, in addition to nine other senior executives, would resign effective Monday to take responsibility for the scandal.
Miki said he first came to suspect the scandal in July.

Senior managing director Shohei Nozawa, who will replace Miki as of today, told the news conference that an urgent task for the brokerage is to restore investors' and shareholders' confidence in the firm.

The current chairman Yukihira added that he had not met Ryuichi Koike, the racketeer at the centre of a payoff scandal that has also ensnared Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Japan's top brokerage, and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, a leading Japanese commercial bank.
Shoji Saotome, who will replace Yukihira as chairman effective today, told the news conference that the brokerage's alleged involvement in the payoff scandal had hurt its business.
He said that, after prosecutors raided Yamaichi offices in July, two corporations asked Yamaichi to leave the underwriting syndicate for their bonds.
Nozawa, the designated president, also said the brokerage's stock broking business was harmed as some corporate clients ceased placing orders with it due to the scandal.
